headline: Approved proceedings to lay out a right-of-way over 120 Spear Street, with a February 10, 2027 site visit and hearing.
summary: A Development Review Board denial started a 120-day deadline for the city to decide whether to acquire the land, so the city began proceedings now. Staff said talks with the property owner will continue. Councilors also discussed a legislative advocacy list and were asked to send their top five policy items by the end of Tuesday.
decisions: Approved instituting proceedings and opening a public hearing on laying out a right-of-way over 120 Spear Street, 4-0.
Approved February 10, 2027 at 3:00 p.m. for a site visit and 5:00 p.m. for the hearing on necessity and compensation, 4-0.

Dr. Zigmund moved to select February 10th at 3:00 p.m. as the date and time for a site visit to examine the premises, and to conduct the public hearing on necessity and compensation or damages at 5:00 p.m. on that date. Mr. Smith seconded. The motion passed 4-0.

decision_titles: Site visit and hearing dates for 120 Spear Street right-of-way
plain_text:
PAGE 1 
DRAFT MINUTES 
SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL 
     6 NOVEMBER 2026 
 
The South Burlington City Council held a special meeting on Friday, 6 November   
2026, at 12:00 PM, in the Auditorium, 180 Market Street, and by Zoom.  
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: T. Barritt, Chair; E. Fitzgerald, L. Smith, A. Chalnick, Dr. B. 
Zigmund 
 
ALSO PRESENT: J. Baker, City Manager; N. Storellicastro, Deputy City Manager; 
C. McNeil, City Attorney; E. Towle, Public Works Director; M. Simoneau; C. 
Chorsa; F. MacDonald; B. Brady; A. Allen 
 
1. Pledge of Allegiance: 
 
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. 
 
2. Instructions on exiting the building in case of emergency and review of 
technology options: 
 
Ms. Baker provided instructions on emergency exit from the building and 
reviewed technology options. 
  
3. Additions, deletions or changes in the order of Agenda items: 
 
No changes were made to the Agenda. 
 
4. Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda: 
 
No issues were raised.
CITY COUNCIL6 NOVEMBER 2026 PAGE 2 
5. Hold a Public Hearing to institute proceedings regarding the laying 
out of right-of-way depicted on Official City Map over 1720 Spear 
Street: 
 
Mr. Chalnick was recused from this hearing due to a potential conflict of interest. 
 
Mr. Storellicastro reviewed the history including the Development Review Board 
(DRB) denial of an application because the appellant had not included the right-of-
way which appears on the Official City Map.  The City had 120 days from that 
denial to determine whether to institute proceedings to acquire the land or an 
interest in the land.  That 120 days expires tomorrow, so the City Council must 
institute those proceedings by today in order to stop the 120-day clock.  The City 
is engaged in very productive discussions with the property owner which will now 
continue. 
 
Mr. McNeil said the agenda asks the Council to consider a step to start the 
proceedings today and formally stop the 120-day clock and set a date for a site 
inspection and a date for a hearing on necessity and compensation and then 
adjourn the meeting to those dates and times. 
 
Dr. Zigmund moved to institute proceedings and open a public hearing to 
schedule examination of premises and a public hearing on necessity and 
compensation/damages for rights to lay out the right-of-way shown one the 
Official City Map over the property known as 120 Spear Street. Mr. Smith 
seconded.  The motion passed 4-0. 
 
Mr. McNeil said the Council should now choose dates for examination of the 
property and the hearing on necessity and damages.  The suggested date is 
Wednesday, 10 February 2027 at 3:00 p.m. for the examination of the premises 
and 10 February 2027 at 5:00 p.m. for the hearing on necessity and 
compensation/damages. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald asked why the dates are so far in the future and at a time of year 
when it may be difficult to access the property.  Mr. McNeil said it is to comply 
with all statutory requirements and to send out property documentation to the 
property owner.  Ms. Baker added it is the City’s hope to reach an agreement 
before that date.  Mr. Smith said he has walked the property many times, and it’s 
always been walkable.
CITY COUNCIL6 NOVEMBER 2026 PAGE 3 
Dr. Zigmund moved to select February 10th at 3:00 p.m. as the date and time for a 
site visit to examine the premises, and to conduct the public hearing on necessity 
and compensation or damages at 5:00 p.m. on that date.  Mr. Smith seconded.  
The motion passed 4-0. 
 
Dr. Zigmund then moved to adjourn the public hearing to the dates and times 
selected for the site visit and public hearing and to direct city staff to abide by all 
notice and other statutory requirements related to the laying out of highways in 
advance of the selected date.  Mr. Smith seconded.  The motion passed 4-0. 
 
Mr. Chalnick rejoined the Council. 
 
6. Consider entering into executive session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. 
Section 313(a)(3) for the purpose of discussing the evaluation of a 
public official and specifically the City Manager: 
 
Mr. Smith moved to enter into executive session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. Section 
313(a)(3) to discuss the evaluation of a public official, specifically the City 
Manager, inviting into the session Ms. Baker and Mr. Storellicastro.  Mr. Chalnick 
seconded.  The motion passed unanimously. 
 
Mr. Smith moved to exit executive session.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  The motion 
passed unanimously. 
 
7. Discussion of legislative advocacy agenda: 
 
Ms. Baker said she hoped the Council could get to a list of issues to strategically 
focus on this biennium.  There should be a final list by the next meeting.  Staff will 
continue to testify on issues of professional expertise.  The Council’s list should be 
policy-based.   
 
Mr. Barritt asked if there are whole categories where there is no chance to make 
changes.  If so, those should be crossed off the list. 
 
Dr. Zigmund asked about the process after the Council creates its list.  Ms. Baker 
said the agreed upon list will be given to the newly elected Legislative delegation 
before they begin to draft legislation.  When the Legislature is in session, staff will 
track these items and/or other related bills.  Ms. Baker noted that the Council had 
talked about some Councilors being “point persons” on specific things, so if 
something came up, that person could talk to staff about it.
CITY COUNCIL6 NOVEMBER 2026 PAGE 4 
Ms. Baker noted that Council recommendations could be specific (e.g., local 
option taxes) or more general (authority to diversify revenue streams).   
 
Mr. Storellicastro said the four areas of advocacy that staff provided are specific to 
South Burlington’s needs.  One way to look at this is that the City will benefit from 
VLCT’s advocacy on a lot of the items on the list, so the Council could look at 
something specific to the City such as reducing the minimum 25 miles per hour 
speed limit. 
 
Dr. Zigmund noted that a lot of the items on the list relate to expanding authority 
for municipalities.  She asked if there are other ways to get that authority without 
passing legislation.  Ms. Baker said this is done through legislation or charter 
changes.   
 
Mr. Barritt said that to him it is about maximizing tax return to the City and 
minimizing costs to the City that the City felt were unfair or unjust.  He added it is 
also about the City’s ability to inspect new construction and finding out where the 
1% local option tax comes from without violating confidentiality. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald said she used the VLCT advocacy agenda which included: 
 
a. Local option tax (current authority and deploying existing revenue 
streams) 
b. Transportation (the apportionment around managing initiatives 
including paving schedules, weights of vehicles, etc.).   
c. Social services/public safety 
d. Housing/energy/economic development 
e. The work for City Clerk’s offices on elections and voter perception 
on how elections were handled (e.g., the large number of returned 
mail ballots for a number of reasons) 
 
Ms. Smith said reducing the 25 miles per hour speed limit which he felt is too fast 
on residential streets.  He was also concerned with affordability, specifically for 
people living in an “economic desert” and who can’t pay bills.  He liked the local 
option tax but said it is a regressive tax in most cases because everyone pays the 
same amount.  He asked how to create progressive income streams through 
taxes/property taxes/inspection fees/other revenue streams that allow for more 
flexibility.  Mr. Barritt noted the City controls inspection fees.
CITY COUNCIL6 NOVEMBER 2026 PAGE 5 
Mr. Barritt suggested staff provide a spread sheet and have Council members 
mark who is of most interest to them. 
 
Ms. Baker said the first set of staff recommendations fall into four categories: 
 
a. Local option taxes 
b. Transportation 
c. Municipal authority on energy codes 
d. E-motos 
 
The “emerging issues” are things staff is keeping an eye on which could become 
concerns in the future (e.g., diversifying revenue streams). 
 
Mr. Storellicastro said staff is thinking about the open meeting law as it relates to 
subcommittee requirements.  Subcommittees now have to follow the full open 
meeting law. He said if there were legislation relative to that, the City would try to 
advocate for something beneficial to the Library Board of Trustees.   
 
Mr. Smith said the open meeting law is different for the City Council and for 
Legislators.  He asked if they could ask to fix that so both operate under the same 
rules.  Ms. Baker noted the Legislature has a lot more flexibility on warning 
meetings, agendas, etc. 
 
Ms. Baker then spoke to the 4 main areas suggested by staff. They could include: 
 
  #1. Advocating for a 2% local option tax similar to Stowe’s – 
changing the charter change process the City would have to go through.  The City 
has ambitious goals and the question is how to get revenue for those things 
without having the property tax as the sole source of funding.  Since the City can’t 
access specific option tax receipts, staff can’t know what would happen if, for 
example, the City added another hotel.  Having that information would help to 
create an economic development strategy.  Mr. Barritt noted this would help other 
municipalities as well. 
 
  #2. Transportation: Ms. Baker said this relates specifically to how the 
State Transportation Fund is allocated for Class 1 Highways.  The formula does 
not take into consideration vehicle miles traveled.  The City could advocate for 
vehicle miles traveled to be part of the criteria for distribution of funding.  There 
could also be more authority for municipalities to use grants for improving 
municipal infrastructure.  Dr. Zigmund expressed surprise that miles traveled is
CITY COUNCIL6 NOVEMBER 2026 PAGE 6 
not already part of the formula.  Ms. Baker said this is political because most 
legislators come from smaller communities where there aren’t high vehicle miles 
traveled.  Mr. Barritt said there will probably be an increase this year on EV fees or 
a “tack on” fee to make up for what the state is not getting from gas/diesel taxes. 
 
  #3. Municipal authority to enforce energy codes: The city could just 
ask to grant this authority or ask for a change in the law so it is clearer.  Mr. 
Chalnick asked if this would apply only to new buildings.   
 
  #4. E-moto sales limitation to dealers: Mr. Barritt said he does not 
favor this as it is a constraint of liberty.  Mr. Smith cited the enforcement issue.  
Ms. Baker said they are not asking that these not be sold; they are saying sell 
them where motor vehicles are sold.  Dr. Zigmund asked how you prevent them 
from being sold on-line.  Ms. Baker said that is why it would be great to have a 
State law.  Mr. Smith said it would require them to be registered at time of sale, 
similar to a motorcycle.  Mr. Barritt cited the “grey area” of off-road usage. 
 
Dr. Zigmund suggested piloting increased municipal authority on a small scale. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald suggested each member provide a list of top 5 policy items.  Ms. 
Baker asked to have these by the end of the day on Tuesday.  
 
8. Other Business: 
 
No other business was presented. 
 
As there was no further business to come before the Council Mr. Smith moved to                   
adjourn.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.  The meeting 
was adjourned at 2:32 p.m.
